s01.text: Millions of people open private browsing windows believing their traffic is completely invisible.

s02.text: In truth, Incognito Mode hides nothing from the internet. It is simply a browser that deletes its own local history file when you close the tab.

s03.text: The second you type a web address, your operating system fires an unencrypted UDP packet on port fifty-three to resolve the domain name.

s04.text: Even under modern HTTPS encryption, the TLS handshake broadcasts the Server Name Indication in plain text across your local Wi-Fi and Internet provider.

s05.text: Commercial tracking networks don't even need cookies: they query your device's graphics card, screen dimensions, and system fonts to generate a unique digital fingerprint.

s06.text: In twenty twenty-four, Google agreed to destroy billions of browsing records to settle a five-billion-dollar lawsuit over tracking Incognito users.

s07.text: Incognito Mode protects you from one person: whoever borrows your physical laptop tomorrow. From the internet, you are in plain sight.
